raw_response:
I will keep my farm simple and manageable this year. I am 76, and although I know farming well after 50 years, I do not want a plan that depends on too much labor or too much risk. Because my land is only 8 mu, my household is small, and some family labor is off-farm, I will focus on the crops and practices I can control well. I have well irrigation, so I will rely on that to stabilize yields, especially for wheat and maize in the wheat-maize system. I will keep most of my land in wheat followed by maize, because that is my main system and gives me steady grain production. I will keep a smaller part in cotton, because I already grow it and I want some cash income, but I will not expand it because cotton needs more management and picking labor. I will use improved or hybrid seed, moderate fertilizer, limited but timely irrigation, and standard pest control. I will avoid overly intensive inputs because at my age I value stability, ease of management, and dependable output more than chasing the highest possible yield.
